gold_assessment.reasoning: Generated facts mention right-hand pins and needles, right arm/leg weakness, and abnormal gait, but do not state the full composite description (unilateral right-hand numbness/pins and needles with some leg weakness and noticeable gait disturbances) as a single HPI fact, nor specify it as the core history as described in the gold fact.

Gold specifies frequency progression from once weekly to daily. Generated HPI only says episodes now occur a couple of times daily, without the earlier weekly frequency or clear progression from weekly to daily.
Gold states that at the time of review the symptoms were not present. No generated fact states that symptoms are absent at the time of consultation.

Gold: prior blood tests for diabetes and cholesterol were normal. Generated HPI-016 states previous cholesterol and diabetes tests were normal (also adds blood pressure), which captures the gold content.
No generated fact addresses absence of past CVA/TIA.
No generated fact states that other past medical or family history is nil of note.

Gold: patient self-medicates with daily aspirin due to family history. Generated med-001 states self-initiated aspirin 75 mg once daily, which encompasses daily self-medication; reason (family history) is implied only in the source text but not needed to cover gold content.
Both gold and generated allergy-001 state patient is allergic to penicillin.
Gold: father had CVA and carotid endarterectomy. Generated fhx-001 only notes surgery to reduce stroke risk without explicitly stating CVA or carotid endarterectomy.
Gold states remaining family history is unremarkable; generated facts do not address this.
Gold: patient is a non-smoker. Generated sh-003 also states non-smoker.
Gold: patient is a medical doctor, plastic surgeon. Generated sh-001: doctor in plastic surgery, equivalent information.
Gold: lives with wife. Generated sh-002: lives with his wife; same content.

Gold assessment explicitly identifies TIAs in a young patient and mentions need to exclude systemic disease such as antiphospholipid syndrome. Generated assessment only states recurrent neurological episodes and TIA as a differential, without the ‘despite young age’ aspect or systemic/antiphospholipid consideration.

Gold: urgent appointment in TIA clinic with referral faxed immediately. Generated plan-001: referral to TIA clinic for urgent assessment. Urgency and referral are captured, though ‘fax now’ detail is omitted but not required for coverage.

Gold: patient to contact TIA clinic via PALS/clinic number to ensure follow-up. Generated fu-001 indicates patient to contact clinic via provided numbers to confirm appointment, but that is in Follow_up_Information; no generated Plan_of_Care item directly restates this plan detail. Under the instructions we assess within each section, so the plan-of-care instruction itself is omitted in the Plan_of_Care section.
Gold: attend A/E if prolonged symptoms occur. Generated plan-002 and plan-004: advise A&E if symptoms persist/do not resolve, and emergency advice if symptoms prolong. This covers the gold content.
Gold: denies dysphagia. Generated hpi-012: no difficulty swallowing. Equivalent negative symptom.
Gold: denies dysphasia. Generated hpi-013: denies difficulty speaking. Equivalent description of dysphasia denial.

Gold: instructed to contact TIA clinic via PALS/clinic number to ensure follow-up. Generated fu-001: patient to contact clinic via provided numbers to confirm appointment. This matches the intent and content.

gen_assessment.reasoning: Chief complaint not described in gold facts; content is consistent but not explicitly supported.

Gold: some leg weakness and gait disturbance with unilateral right-hand symptoms. Generated: perceived weakness in the right arm. This is consistent with unilateral limb weakness, although gold highlights leg; still within the same neurological picture and not contradictory.
Resolution after a few days for pins and needles/weakness is not specified in gold facts.
